Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Town, shops & places

centre noun

a building for an activity

also center, sports centre, health centre, community centre, visitor centre, information centre, facility

modern

M-O s.v. tourist office, information office, visitors’ center: sēdēs nūntiātiōnum, citing Egger
M-O s.v. office: officiōrum sēdēs, citing Egger

sēdēs, sēdis f.

noun, third declension

with a genitive, the seat of an activity: a centre, an office

Classically a seat or dwelling, the place where something has its home (Lewis & Short). Where Latin has a name for the place, use it: a sports centre is a gymnasium, a health centre a valētūdinārium (see gym, hospital).

Other words

  • conciliābulum, conciliābulī n. — a meeting place; a community or conference centre

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Liv. 25.5.6 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. convention center

    In Livy the market and meeting place of a country district. Plautus uses it as a joke for a brothel (Trin. 2.2.38, Lewis & Short).

See also gym, hospital, day care, shopping mall, library, centre.

SourcesLewis & Short: sedes · Lewis & Short: conciliabulum

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. office; tourist office, information office, visitors’ center; convention center.
